# /response/[id]

The detail view for one drawing: the prompt it answered, who made it, when,
the drawing itself, and a heart reaction. It is where a wall grid tile opens
into and where the outbound share flow begins.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Route | `/response/[id]` |
| Router file | `app/response/[id].tsx` |
| Flows | F5 Wall browsing, reactions and composition; F6 Share outside the app (`product/design/screen-flow-inventory.md:182`, `:111`, `:122`) |
| Position in flow | F5 leaf reached from `/family`; the entry point to F6 via the share button (`product/design/screen-flow-inventory.md:376-378`) |
| Data calls | one read, `getResponse`; one write, `addReaction`; plus a supporting `listChannelDays` read for prompt text |
| Shared surface | `EnhancedToggleImage` / `DrawingImage`, also used on wall and share tiles |

Cited to hs2studio/scribl-app at `c1b3c2d` on `main`, clean tree.

## The capture

<figure class="tile-single"><a href="/assets/prototype/21-response.png"><img src="/assets/prototype/21-response.png" alt="Response detail: the prompt 'Draw what your name would look like as a creature', author Rob on Family Wall at 11:10 AM, a white card holding an orange sun-and-rays glyph, a caption reading 'Sketching the sunrise over the backyard fence', and a heart reaction chip showing 2"></a><figcaption>Open the tile. From <code>npm run capture:board</code> at scribl-app <code>72c3ab8</code>, captured 2026-08-31.</figcaption></figure>

This tile does not show what the inventory's Finding 3 describes. Finding 3
says the artwork panel renders as a solid black rectangle
(`product/design/screen-flow-inventory.md:244-250`). This capture shows an
orange sun-and-rays glyph on a white card, fully visible, not black. Prompt,
author, timestamp, caption, and the reaction chip all render too, matching the
part of Finding 3 that says those render fine.

The source rules out the "Skia not painting on web" half of Finding 3's guess
for this screen specifically: the artwork here is a plain `<Image>` reading a
data-URI `imageRef`, not a Skia canvas (`components/DrawingImage.tsx:36-40`,
composed through `components/EnhancedToggleImage.tsx:63-65`). There is no Skia
surface on this route to fail to paint. That leaves the other half of the
finding, that the seeded response carries no strokes, as the only remaining
candidate for a black-panel capture, and it did not reproduce here: this
capture's `imageRef` decoded to a real (if wrong) glyph. The sun glyph is the
same placeholder art called out in the F2 workflow page's note on
`/onboarding/story` (`product/prototype/workflows/f2-first-run-onboarding.md:169-176`),
which points at the seed data carrying a stock image rather than a captured
drawing, not at a rendering failure. Whether the `main`-branch capture the
inventory read actually shows black, or showed something else that got
misread, is not something this page can settle from `72c3ab8`; Finding 3
should be re-checked against a fresh `main` capture before anyone repeats the
"artwork panel is black" claim.

## Features

| Feature | Where it lives |
|---------|----------------|
| Read the prompt text for this response's own promptId | `app/response/[id].tsx:100-116` |
| View the drawing, or the AI-enhanced version if ready, with an original/enhanced toggle pill | `app/response/[id].tsx:80`, `:327-341`, toggle logic `components/EnhancedToggleImage.tsx:56-61` |
| See the author's name, avatar, and wall/time label | `app/response/[id].tsx:312-324` |
| Play a voice-note response, if this response is audio rather than text | `app/response/[id].tsx:367-372` |
| Read the caption, if this response is text rather than audio | `app/response/[id].tsx:373-377` |
| React with a single heart chip, toggled on and off | `app/response/[id].tsx:214-222`, chip built at `:157-174` |
| Author-only: edit the AI background prompt and save it | `app/response/[id].tsx:382-416`, gated on `isOwner && AI_ENABLED` |
| Author-only: regenerate the AI background | `app/response/[id].tsx:417-421`, handler `:199-212` |
| Share out via the header button, which opens `/share` | `app/response/[id].tsx:230-268` |
| Retry the load on error | `app/response/[id].tsx:296-301` |

Text and audio are mutually exclusive server-side, enforced by a DB CHECK
noted in a comment at `app/response/[id].tsx:363-366`; `hasAudio` is the
switch (`app/response/[id].tsx:180`). The AI toggle, background-prompt editor,
and regenerate button are all gated behind the `AI_ENABLED` kill-switch
(`app/response/[id].tsx:20`, `:80`, `:382`), so with AI off this screen shows
only the drawing, author, caption, and reaction. The reaction control itself
was narrowed from three emoji sets to one heart, stated directly in a comment
at `app/response/[id].tsx:163-165`, because the wall grid only ever offered a
single heart and the detail view offering three made one drawing reactable
three different ways depending which screen you reacted from.

A locked state exists for a response reached before the viewer has submitted
today's drawing: a plain message, no retry, no bypass (`app/response/[id].tsx:285-291`).
The screen renders that state rather than gating locally, per the component
doc comment at `app/response/[id].tsx:44-49`.

## Data calls

| Client method | Endpoint | Handler |
|---------------|----------|---------|
| `getResponse(channelId, promptId, responseId)` | `GET /channels/{channelId}/responses?promptId=...` | `backend/lambda/handlers/channel-responses.ts` |
| `addReaction(channelId, promptId, responseId, emoji)` | `POST /channels/{channelId}/responses/{responseId}/reactions?promptId=...` | `backend/lambda/handlers/reaction-add.ts` |
| `listChannelDays(channelId)` | `GET /channels/{channelId}/days` | `backend/lambda/handlers/channel-days.ts` |

The client methods are `getResponse` at `src/data/http.ts:194-207` and
`addReaction` at `src/data/http.ts:229-244`. The screen does not call either
directly; both go through `useResponseDetailStore` (`app/response/[id].tsx:58-68`),
loaded on an effect keyed on `channelId`, `promptId`, and `id`
(`app/response/[id].tsx:133-135`), and the reaction fired from `toggleReaction`
(`app/response/[id].tsx:214-222`). `getResponse` fetches the whole day's
response list and finds the one matching `responseId` client-side
(`src/data/http.ts:198-206`); there is no single-response GET endpoint.

`addReaction`'s handler writes the reaction in place and returns the updated
response (`backend/lambda/handlers/reaction-add.ts:128`), which the store
writes straight into `data` rather than triggering a reload, so reacting does
not flash the full-screen spinner (comment at `app/response/[id].tsx:218-220`).

A second, unrelated read resolves the prompt text: `listChannelDays(channelId)`
is called directly from the screen (`app/response/[id].tsx:103-108`), and the
result is matched against `promptId` rather than derived from a date, because
a pack-injected prompt's id is not `prompt-YYYY-MM-DD` shaped
(`app/response/[id].tsx:93-98`).

## State in, state out

**Reads on entry.** `channelId`, `promptId`, and `id` from route params
(`app/response/[id].tsx:53-57`), then the response detail store's `data`,
`loading`, `error`, and `locked` (`app/response/[id].tsx:58-63`).

**Writes on mount.** Triggers `load(channelId, promptId, id)` when all three
params are present (`app/response/[id].tsx:133-135`), and `loadWalls()` to
resolve the channel's display name (`app/response/[id].tsx:137-139`, name
lookup at `:152`).

**Writes on exit.** None to a store. Reacting writes to the server and back
into `data` in place (`app/response/[id].tsx:214-222`); there is no local
draft or param write on navigating away. Pressing share pushes the full
response payload as route params to `/share`
([`/share`](/prototype/screens/share)), rather than writing to a store
(`app/response/[id].tsx:239-267`).

`EnhancedToggleImage` and `DrawingImage` are the same pair used to render
drawings on the wall grid and on `/share`; a comment on `DrawingImage`
describes it as "kept tiny and reused across wall/family/response/share
screens" (`components/DrawingImage.tsx:16`).

## Notes for planning

Authored here, not read out of the app.

### Finding 3 does not reproduce on this capture, and the source rules out one of its two guesses

The inventory's black-artwork finding is either stale or was reading a
different failure than what this route actually does. This screen has no
Skia canvas at all: the drawing is a plain `<Image>` on a data-URI
(`components/DrawingImage.tsx:36-40`). So "Skia not painting on web" cannot be
the cause here, whatever it is on `/draw` or `/onboarding/canvas`. The
remaining candidate, an empty-strokes seed, is plausible in general but this
particular capture had real (if wrong) image data. Before anyone repeats
Finding 3 in a client-facing document, it needs a fresh look against a `main`
capture with the actual failing seed, not a restatement from this page.

### The sun glyph is a seed-data problem, not a rendering problem, and it is the second sighting

The F2 workflow page's note 2 already flags the same sun-and-rays glyph
appearing where a person's own drawing should be, on `/onboarding/story`
(`product/prototype/workflows/f2-first-run-onboarding.md:169-176`). It shows
up again here, on a completely different screen and a completely different
data path (`getResponse` versus a local draft store). That is not a
coincidence worth ignoring: it points at one shared placeholder image getting
seeded wherever a real drawing capture wasn't wired up, rather than two
unrelated bugs. Worth tracing to its one seed source before treating it as
two tickets.

### The reaction chip narrowing is a documented product decision, unlike most narrowings in this app

Most reductions in this codebase (see the onboarding canvas's unexplained
palette) are silent. This one has its reasoning written directly into the
code as a comment (`app/response/[id].tsx:163-165`): three reaction sets
collapsed to one heart because the wall grid only ever offered one. That is
the standard this repo should hold every other narrowing to.
